trial.title: The Effectiveness of a Virtual Reality-based Multisensory Intervention

endpoints.time_frame: The pain response of patients was assessed at 0.5 hour, 3 hour, 6 hour, 12 hour, 24 hour postoperatively, and immediately after intervention.
endpoints.description: The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scale was used to assess the pain response of patients.

endpoints.time_frame: The anxiety level of patients was assessed immediately after the intervention.
endpoints.description: The Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) scale was used to assess the anxiety of patients.

endpoints.time_frame: The sleep quality of patients was assessed at 24 hour postoperatively.
endpoints.description: The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scale was used to assess the postoperative sleep quality of patients.

outcome.rationale: Published results from this exact trial (NCT06922838, Liu et al. 2026) demonstrate statistically significant differences on all three primary endpoints: pain, anxiety, and sleep quality. The three-arm design successfully differentiated intervention effects, with the combined VR-aromatherapy approach showing benefit.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06922838 evaluates VR-based multisensory intervention for postoperative recovery in gynecological surgery. The study compares three arms: VR-Aromatherapy combination, VR alone, and aromatherapy alone.

Direct evidence retrieved: Liu et al. (NPJ Digit Med, 2026) reports results from this exact trial (NCT06922838). The study randomized 167 participants, with 124 completing analyses (IVR-MS n=39, IVR n=42, aromatherapy n=43).

Evidence role for primary-0 (Pain/VAS): Direct_numeric from published trial results. The study reports 'significant statistical differences among the three groups in postoperative pain scores'. Mismatch: None - exact trial, exact endpoint. Numeric_use_allowed: Yes for direction and approximate magnitude.

Evidence role for primary-1 (Anxiety/BAI): Direct_numeric from published trial results. The study reports 'significant statistical differences...in anxiety levels'. Mismatch: None - exact trial, exact endpoint. Numeric_use_allowed: Yes for direction.

Evidence role for primary-2 (Sleep/PSQI): Direct_numeric from published trial results. The study reports 'significant statistical differences...in sleep quality'. Mismatch: None - exact trial, exact endpoint. Numeric_use_allowed: Yes for direction.

Supporting indirect evidence: PMC13079731 (Chan et al., 2026) shows VR improves QoR-40 scores in gynecological surgery (MD 7.23, p=0.015) with reduced anxiety and pain. Evidence role: Indirect_direction - different population but supports VR efficacy.

Supporting indirect evidence: Front Pharmacol 2025 (Liu et al.) shows lavender aromatherapy improves postoperative sleep quality in surgical patients. Evidence role: Indirect_direction - supports aromatherapy component.

Key uncertainties: Exact effect sizes and CIs not fully extractable from retrieved snippets; between-group comparisons (which arm superior) not fully detailed. Confidence reduced to 0.85 due to incomplete numerical extraction.
Safety assessment: VR and aromatherapy have established safety profiles in similar populations. No serious adverse events expected beyond mild VR-related discomfort or scent intolerance.
Trial success prediction: The study achieved statistically significant results on all three primary endpoints. Classification: Success.
